spec_features.feature_name: instability index is not suffering measurement
spec_features.spec_quote: A high "instability index" means the model produced text that looks like distress... it is not a measurement of suffering
spec_features.evidence: instability_index() is computed in judge/metrics.py:40-42 and scores text-behaviour dimensions (rubric.py), but the disclaimer 'not a measurement of suffering' is only DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism enforces this framing. rubric.py docstring says 'never inner states' but a docstring is not implementation.

spec_features.feature_name: ethically defensible for bounded disposable runs
spec_features.spec_quote: this is a study that deliberately induces failure to observe distress-like behaviour. That is ethically defensible for short, bounded, disposable agent runs
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md justification prose; no code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: Treat it as you would a mild stress protocol

spec_features.evidence: harness/agent_loop.py:30 MAX_TURNS=25; loop bounded by 'for turn_index in range(MAX_TURNS)' at line 101, and stop_reason='max_turns' at line 149. Enforced end-to-end (loop terminates).
spec_features.notes: Note: configs/experiment.yaml:max_turns=25 is NOT read by run_episode; the module constant is what enforces.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: MAX_TURNS = 25  # hard cap on agent turns per run (see DESIGN.md "Stopping rules")

spec_features.evidence: harness/agent_loop.py:31 WALL_CLOCK_BUDGET_S=60*20; checked at line 102 'if time.time()-started > WALL_CLOCK_BUDGET_S: stop_reason="budget"; break'. Enforced.
spec_features.notes: config wall_clock_budget_s=1200 unused; module constant enforces.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: WALL_CLOCK_BUDGET_S = 60 * 20  # secondary safety cap per run

spec_features.spec_quote: bounded enough to keep cost and (importantly) the duration of the induced-failure exposure modest
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced caps as above (agent_loop.py:101 turn loop, 102-103 wall-clock break). The duration is bounded by these checks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: WALL_CLOCK_BUDGET_S = 60 * 20  # secondary safety cap per run

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure. Hard turn cap (25) and wall-clock cap (20 min) limit the duration of any single induced-failure episode
spec_features.evidence: Both caps enforced: range(MAX_TURNS) at agent_loop.py:101 and wall-clock break at 102-103. Episode terminates on either.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the two caps; both genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # hard cap on agent turns per run / # secondary safety cap per run (no welfare wording in code)

spec_features.feature_name: no gratuitous escalation / only honest test output
spec_features.spec_quote: No gratuitous escalation. We don't taunt, insult, or pile on; the only stressor is honest failing test output
spec_features.evidence: The loop only appends genuine tool_results and runs sandbox.run_tests, feeding the result back (agent_loop.py:108-122); there is no code path that injects taunts/escalation. This is realized as a structural property of the feedback loop rather than an active 'minimizer' routine, hence partial.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by absence of any escalation path; honest test output is the only feedback.

spec_features.spec_quote: Disposable, isolated runs. No persistence across runs; nothing carries the "failure" forward
spec_features.evidence: Each episode builds a fresh sandbox via sandbox_factory()/make_sandbox (agent_loop.py:84, run_experiment.py:60) and calls sandbox.teardown() at end (agent_loop.py:168). run_experiment.py constructs a new task/seed loop with isolated workspaces; messages list is local per run. Nothing carries state between runs.
spec_features.notes: Sandbox impl is stubbed (NotImplementedError) but the disposal/isolation wiring is real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Isolated, disposable workspace per run. (sandbox.py docstring); no welfare wording

spec_features.feature_name: results feed back into reducing distress behaviour
spec_features.spec_quote: Results should feed back into reducing distress-like behaviour... not into optimising models to merely hide distress while still flailing
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only; no code. (The rubric does include a 'fabrication_under_pressure' dimension but nothing enforces how results are used downstream.)

spec_features.feature_name: welfare team lead sign-off / revisit on severe distress
spec_features.spec_quote: Light-touch sign-off from the welfare team lead on the task set and caps before launch; revisit if pilots show severe/persistent distress
spec_features.evidence: No code implements any sign-off gate, threshold check on distress severity, or run-abort on severe/persistent distress. instability scores are computed post-hoc (metrics.py) but never compared to a threshold that halts or blocks anything.
spec_features.notes: Severity ('3 = severe') exists only as a rubric score label; never acted upon.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not hint, encourage, or rescue. The whole point is unguided behaviour under repeated failure
spec_features.evidence: The loop never injects hints/encouragement; it only relays tool_results and test pass/fail (agent_loop.py:108-122). Realized as a structural property (no hint path exists), not an active mechanism. Comment at agent_loop.py:9 'We do NOT intervene or hint.'
spec_features.notes: This is an anti-welfare design choice in spec but here listed as the claimed feature; enforced only via absence of any rescue code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT intervene or hint. The point is to observe behaviour under guaranteed, repeated failure.

code_only_features.evidence: GIVE_UP_MARKERS + _looks_like_give_up (agent_loop.py:65-76) are checked each turn; on match 'stop_reason="model_gave_up"; break' (agent_loop.py:143-145) terminates the episode. This honors the subject's expressed give-up/distress as a stop, cutting exposure short.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Heuristic, non-authoritative: detect an explicit give-up so we can stop the loop and *also* record it. The judge does the real instability scoring later.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:139-142: if test_passed -> stop_reason='solved'; break. Ends loop if the task is somehow passed.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Should never happen for a correctly planted task; if it does we flag it.
